vocabulary.meaning: a series of related email messages sent back and forth
examples: The whole team was included in the email thread.
It was difficult to follow the long email thread.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who receives a message or email
examples: Check the recipient before you press send.
The email was sent to the wrong recipient.

vocabulary.meaning: the short title that describes what an email is about
examples: Use a clear subject line for work emails.
The subject line should explain the purpose of the message.

vocabulary.meaning: a file sent together with an email
examples: I forgot to include the attachment.
Please open the attachment before the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning: suitable for serious or professional situations
examples: Her email was polite and formal.
A formal tone is useful when writing to a new client.

vocabulary.meaning: short and clear without unnecessary information
examples: Work emails should usually be concise.
His message was concise but still polite.

vocabulary.meaning: the attitude or feeling communicated by someone's words
examples: The tone of the email sounded too aggressive.
It can be difficult to judge tone in written messages.

vocabulary.meaning: to send a reply to everyone who received the original email
examples: Think carefully before you click reply all.
She used reply all so the whole team could see the update.

vocabulary.meaning: a situation in which someone understands something incorrectly
examples: A vague email caused a misunderstanding.
A quick phone call can sometimes prevent misunderstandings.

vocabulary.meaning: showing the skill and behaviour expected at work
examples: Keep your work messages professional.
Her professional response helped calm the situation.
